notes: Step 1 unjustifiably infers independent fair sexes from population balance and intra-family independence. Counterexample: take two 2-child families. In the first, sexes are independent with P(boy)=1/4; the second family's sexes are coordinatewise complements of the first's. Each family has independent sexes, and the population always contains exactly two boys and two girls. Nevertheless, E[brothers|female]=3/8 and E[brothers|male]=5/8. Replicating these blocks gives arbitrarily large populations satisfying the stated assumptions.
